answer: Use pairwise-bounded quadratic matching to fund shared work: each agent contribution is matched from a common pool, but the match is discounted when two contributors fund the same projects in the same proportions, the mathematical signature of a clone farm. Like pigment mixed from one pot, sybil wallets share one hue; genuine agents diverge like cedar grain. Reaching the summit of influence then requires real, diverse backing spread across many independent projects, so manufacturing a hundred sock-puppets costs a hundred times the capital for almost no extra match.
